summary: Alignment helper for UI/texture positioning. Given a base point (a1=x, a2=y), an extent (a3=width, a4=height) and an alignment selector a5, computes an anchored position into output pointers *a6 (x) and *a7 (y). Nine selectors (0..8) produce combinations of left/right/center X anchoring and top/bottom/center Y anchoring via the jump table jpt_4DC350. Returns a6 for case 0, a7 for cases 1..8, and the raw selector a5 (as a pointer) for the default branch.

operations.description: Initialize result to a5, the alignment selector value, before dispatch.
Dispatch on alignment selector a5 via the jump table jpt_4DC350 into cases 0..8.
Case 0: top-left anchor — *a6 = a1, *a7 = a2; return a6.
Case 1: right-top anchor — *a6 = a1 - a3, *a7 = a2; return a7.
Case 2: center-top anchor — *a6 = a1 - a3/2, *a7 = a2; return a7.
Cases 3 and 5: bottom anchor — *a7 = a2 - a4; case 5 additionally centers X via a1 -= a3/2 while case 3 keeps *a6 = a1; both return a7.
Case 4: right-bottom anchor — *a6 = a1 - a3, *a7 = a2 - a4; return a7.
Cases 6, 7 and 8: vertical center anchor — *a7 = a2 - a4/2; X is a1 (case 6), a1 - a3 (case 7), or a1 - a3/2 (case 8); all return a7.
Default branch returns the raw selector a5 cast to a pointer; recognized cases return a6 (case 0) or a7 (cases 1..8).

clean_pseudocode: _DWORD* sub_4DC340(int x, int y, int w, int h, unsigned align, _DWORD* outX, _DWORD* outY) {
case 1: *outX = x - w;   *outY = y;       return outY;
case 2: *outX = x - w/2; *outY = y;       return outY;
case 3: *outX = x;       *outY = y - h;   return outY;
case 4: *outX = x - w;   *outY = y - h;   return outY;
case 5: *outX = x - w/2; *outY = y - h;   return outY;
case 6: *outX = x;       *outY = y - h/2; return outY;
case 7: *outX = x - w;   *outY = y - h/2; return outY;
case 8: *outX = x - w/2; *outY = y - h/2; return outY;
return (_DWORD*)align; /* default returns the selector unchanged */
unresolved: The exact UI meaning of alignment values 0..8 is inferred from the anchor arithmetic; callers ScaledTextureRender and TextRenderDispatcher determine how each slot maps to a concrete UI element.
Return value contract is inconsistent across cases (a6, a7, or the raw selector); callers appear to ignore it.
Whether a3/2 and a4/2 are intended as signed division depends on caller invariants (widths/heights assumed positive).
